The *Bhikkhādāyakavimānavatthu* (Vv 70), rendered in English as "Almsfood Giver’s Mansion," is a verse text included in the *Vimānavatthu* collection of the Pali Tipiṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The text recounts how a *deva* gained bountiful celestial rewards and a heavenly abode as a consequence of offering water to a thirsty monk [SuttaCentral]. Four modern translations across four languages are documented on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral].

No external parallels in Chinese Āgamas, Sanskrit, or Tibetan literature are recorded by SuttaCentral or identified by DharmaNexus [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. However, DharmaNexus reveals substantial internal Pali text reuse, registering 154 matches across 23 texts [DharmaNexus]. The commentary, *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, forms the largest textual partner, covering segments §1.1–5.3 [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, recurring formulaic descriptions and verse units (such as §1.4–4.1/4.2) are shared widely with other poems within the *Vimānavatthu*, including the *Guttilavimānavatthu* (Vv 33), *Phaladāyakavimānavatthu* (Vv 67), *Paṭhamakuṇḍalīvimānavatthu* (Vv 72), *Sunikkhittavimānavatthu* (Vv 85), *Dutiyakuṇḍalīvimānavatthu* (Vv 73), and *(Uttara) Pāyāsivimānavatthu* (Vv 74) [DharmaNexus].
